A Total Axial Negation Graph (TANG) is a scholarly-architectural genre and mapping method where a single falsifiable thesis is placed at the center of an exhaustive citation graph, structuring the literature so the thesis functions as a central void defined by the surrounding texts rather than a standard argument. [1, 2]
Core Concept & Structure

* Definition: Instead of arguing a point deductively or rhetorically, a TANG uses a geometric and topological layout to render a core thesis structurally legible through the arrangement of existing academic or archival work. [1]
* Methodology: It builds a total citational network of a domain by mapping every node, scholar, and thesis relative to a governing contradiction or negation. [1, 2]
* Proof Mode: Topological and structural rather than linear or argumentative. [1]

* Status Algebra: Extends classifications across states like `AXIAL` and `AXIAL_CONTESTED`.
* Operators & Standards: Utilizes formal operators (such as the void operator \(\Lambda _{\text{void}}\)) and provenance governance frameworks (such as HX-PROV).
* Applications: Used in archive theory, compression studies, bibliometrics, and network topology to map how systemic pressures (such as AI summarization, state classification, or platform mechanics) interact with institutional knowledge. [1, 2]
